purpose: Problem-family assimilation routines between Core (1A) concept teaching and Revised Core (2) transfer.

transfer_routines.title: Velocity components at one instant
recognition_signals: launch speed and launch angle are given
horizontal or vertical component is asked for
one instant may be shared by x and y descriptions

method_steps.title: Draw and fix the axes
method_steps.learner_move: Show where the launch angle is measured and choose +x, +y and the sign of gravity.

method_steps.title: Resolve the launch
method_steps.learner_move: Write u_x=u cos(theta) and u_y=u sin(theta) from the component triangle.

method_steps.title: Ask what changes with time
method_steps.learner_move: Keep v_x=u_x and update v_y=u_y-gt when the question refers to a later instant.

method_steps.title: Use the same clock and check
method_steps.learner_move: Use the same t in both directions, state the requested component/state, and check the sign and magnitude physically.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile is launched at 50 m/s at 37 degrees. Use sin37=0.60, cos37=0.80 and g=10 m/s^2. At t=2 s, find v_x, v_y, x and y.
independent_practice.answer_check: u_x=40 m/s, u_y=30 m/s; at t=2 s, v_x=40 m/s, v_y=10 m/s, x=80 m, y=40 m.

hint_ladder.label: What is the key physics?
hint_ladder.prompt: The same projectile is described in x and y at the same instant; gravity does not change horizontal velocity.

hint_ladder.label: How would you represent it?
hint_ladder.prompt: Use u_x=u cos(theta), u_y=u sin(theta), a_x=0 and a_y=-g on one component diagram.

hint_ladder.label: What would you write first?
hint_ladder.prompt: Start by resolving the launch: u_x=50(0.80), u_y=50(0.60).

readiness_checks: recognise a component-motion question from its givens
draw the component model and accelerations without looking
choose the first useful component equation without a hint
finish a fresh problem without H2 or H3
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Core (2) Q10 only after the learner can recognise, represent, start and finish the routine; hold Q43 until M2D-SBA-04 teaches the apex event.

transfer_routines.title: Velocity direction / horizontal event
recognition_signals: direction or angle of velocity is asked
velocity becomes horizontal at a stated time
a later horizontal event must be used to work backward

method_steps.title: Write the current components
method_steps.learner_move: Keep v_x constant and update v_y with gravity.

method_steps.title: Check for a special event
method_steps.learner_move: Horizontal velocity means v_y=0; a later horizontal event identifies the apex.

method_steps.title: Turn components into direction
method_steps.learner_move: Use tan(phi)=v_y/v_x with the current signs.

method_steps.title: Interpret and check
method_steps.learner_move: State above/horizontal/below and check the event timing.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile has constant horizontal velocity 20 m/s. Its velocity becomes horizontal at t=3.0 s. With g=10 m/s^2, find the velocity angle at t=1.0 s.
independent_practice.answer_check: v_y(1)=20 m/s, v_x=20 m/s, so phi=45 degrees above horizontal.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: A horizontal velocity at t=3 s means v_y=0 there.

readiness_checks: recognise a direction/horizontal-event question
write current components and mark v_y=0 for a horizontal event
choose whether to calculate v_y now or work backward from a later apex
finish a fresh R1 problem without H2 or H3
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q11 and Q17 after 4/4 readiness without H2/H3.

transfer_routines.title: Perpendicular velocity
recognition_signals: velocity becomes perpendicular to initial velocity
an explicit 90 degree condition appears between two velocity vectors

method_steps.title: Write both velocity vectors
method_steps.learner_move: Represent initial u and later v(t) in components.

method_steps.title: Translate 90 degrees
method_steps.learner_move: Use the zero dot-product condition.

method_steps.title: Substitute before simplifying
method_steps.learner_move: Multiply matching components and add.

method_steps.title: Solve and check
method_steps.learner_move: Solve for t and check that it is a positive physical event.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile is launched with u=(9 i + 12 j) m/s. With g=10 m/s^2, find the first time its velocity is perpendicular to its initial velocity.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: The condition is between two perpendicular velocity vectors, not v_y=0.

readiness_checks: distinguish perpendicular from apex/horizontal
write u and v(t) as component pairs
translate perpendicular into u dot v(t)=0 without a hint
solve and physically check a fresh R2 event
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q01 and Q13 after 4/4 readiness without H2/H3.

transfer_routines.title: Speed at a given height
recognition_signals: speed is asked at a specified height
height is a fraction of maximum height

method_steps.title: Separate horizontal and vertical
method_steps.learner_move: Keep v_x=u_x and use height only in vertical motion.

method_steps.title: Use no-time vertical relation
method_steps.learner_move: Write v_y^2=u_y^2-2gy.

method_steps.title: Use the maximum-height condition
method_steps.learner_move: At apex 2gH=u_y^2; at H/2 get v_y^2=u_y^2/2.

method_steps.title: Rebuild total speed and compare
method_steps.learner_move: Use v^2=v_x^2+v_y^2 and compare squared speeds.

independent_practice.prompt: At half maximum height an ideal projectile has speed sqrt(5/8) times launch speed. Find the launch angle.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: At H/2, v_y^2=u_y^2/2 while v_x is unchanged.

hint_ladder.label: First move
hint_ladder.prompt: Square the ratio and set the squared-speed fraction equal to 5/8.

readiness_checks: recognise when height rather than time is the useful variable
write the no-time relation and keep v_x constant
turn H/2 into v_y^2=u_y^2/2
solve a fresh speed-ratio problem with squared components
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q40 after 4/4 readiness without H2/H3.

transfer_routines.title: Apex / minimum-speed cross-bucket bridge
recognition_signals: speed at apex is given as a fraction of launch speed
the question continues into range or height

method_steps.title: Identify the apex speed
method_steps.learner_move: Use v_apex=v_min=u cos(theta).

method_steps.title: Turn a speed ratio into an angle
method_steps.learner_move: Translate v_apex/u into cos(theta).

method_steps.title: Stop at the bucket boundary
method_steps.learner_move: Do not import range/height formulas before SBA-05.

method_steps.title: Release after SBA-05
method_steps.learner_move: Attach the correct same-height relation only after the next bucket.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile has minimum speed 0.6u. Find the launch-angle relation you can determine without any range formula.
independent_practice.answer_check: cos(theta)=0.6, so theta=cos^-1(0.6); stop before range/height work.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Minimum speed occurs at apex where v_y=0.

hint_ladder.label: First move
hint_ladder.prompt: Write u cos(theta)=0.6u and isolate cos(theta).

readiness_checks: identify apex/minimum-speed language
write v_apex=u cos(theta)
turn a speed ratio into an angle
stop before using same-height range/height formulas
transfer_routines.release_rule: Hold Q14 and Q27 until M2D-SBA-05 is complete.
